"They're two of the most memorable episodes of television I've seen, and both are shows by the same creator, but in what I feel is an increasingly post-deconstructionist media landscape, it's the episode whose humanity shines through that resonates the more strongly, for me. 💚"

"In "Community," meanwhile, the plot is resolved when Abed rejects the chaos of creating alternate timelines in favor of holding onto what he finds constant in the world, his friends. The episode ends with a dance party. HTTPURL"
"I think these episodes show that deconstruction is well and good, but a story that lasts uses those tools to say something that resonates."

"Both episodes are clever and funny and had good jokes. But a decade beyond the explosion of postmodern and deconstructive fiction present in that era of television, the R&M episode holds up significantly less well than the Community one."

"(This mirrors the sitcom writer's conundrum: how do you write a compelling story in a very short runtime, when you're expected to return to the status quo by episode's end? And yet, as with sitcom seasons, this episode manages it several times over.)"

"(Tangent: this is a different writing problem from Groundhog Day, which keeps one character consistent throughout all the timelines. "Remedial Chaos Theory" successfully builds a narrative without a single character bringing information between timelines.)"

"Meanwhile the Community episode constructs a coherent narrative (with buildup, running gags, peaks and valleys, and a final denouement and climax) within a structure that eschews temporal consistency. In other words, how do you write a story if time keeps being reset?"

"Both episodes are a deconstruction of a sitcom trope. The R&M episode questions the legitimacy of stories that happen outside the viewer's awareness of them by introducing a large number of side characters, all of which turn out to be not real at all, but in fact evil parasites."

"Recently, I revisited my favorite episode each of two Dan Harmon-created shows. (Disclaimer: I've only ever seen a few episodes from each show.)  "Remedial Chaos Theory" from Community held up far better than "Total Rickall" from Rick & Morty, and I think I know why. HTTPURL"
